I highly recommend this game to new players of the series, or veterans from the Men of War series. This is a full review for the game.

Gates of Hell: Ostfront is probably the best RTS game ever created, especially in filling the WWII genre.  It is a very detailed game where you will command small or large armies of infantry, artillery and armor where you can direct control single units from those armies in third/first person (which is an amazing feature). The historical accuracy in this game is far better than any other WWII game out there. Filled with great details, especially on the armor (such as the jumbo able to be shot through the MG port) which makes it incredibly immersive and fun (or annoying) to play. 

While it still has the old bones from the GEM engine which can create some jank, the amazing developers of BarbedWire managed to (mostly) cover these up by updating the engine and reworking mechanics. The game features singleplayer campaign/skirmishes which have pretty detailed missions with some of them being unique and hard (Legend of Krasny Bor), with each nation having their own detailed campaign on the fronts they fought on. It also has a multiplayer, where there is a good amount of gametypes where you can play pve or pvp - also featuring a doctrine system which allows you to use unique units to that doctrine, infinite replayability (Just be aware, random games can be unstable or toxic to new players). But one of the biggest reasons where hours can be sunk into, is the GEM editor which comes with game. In the editor you can do basically anything you want, set up small battles or create huge ones (which will tank performance). Countless hours will be spent here if that is your sort of thing. 

Performance is good on this game (except on huge city maps, Waal bridge) and remains smooth constantly. Huge explosions can tank it a little bit (especially if lots of trees are blown up) but other than that it remains consistent (unless your on a potatoe). Bugs and glitches are rare but can very annoying, most of this is due to the very old GEM engine which can create some jank, so be aware that annoying things (like a soldier getting stuck in a small area which they vaulted into) can happen. So far I have yet to encounter a game-breaking bug.

Lastly, there are a lot of DLC for this game. Some of which I am not sure if they should of been DLC (Jagdtiger should be base game), but they are worth the price especially on sale. There will be more DLC to come (hopefully it will the African campaign or the Pacific theatre), so keep that in mind. Some of the mods in this game (like MACE) basically are dlcs as they add quality content for free from the Steam workshop, so definetly try those out once you get the grips of the game. 

Thats about all I can really say (without making a proper essay) of this game. It is a truly incredible game where the devs are very passionate about it and the WWII setting it is. While there are small little issues, the pros definetly outweigh them, but I am hopeful they may be addresed. I hope this game gets more popular as it deserves to be, it is a hidden gem. So, yes I recommend this game to RTS enjoyers or people who want try something new (or MOW veterans).

As far as RTS games go, CtA:GoH definitely fits its own niche. Between the ability to manually control units, to battles actually having pacing due to unit economy, it definitely is in a league of its own. If you've played the other Men of War games, it's an absolute step-up above those in terms of quality and features. If you've played the original Call to Arms, it's all of that but more refined and with more features. Not to mention it has mod support through Steam Workshop for whatever fits your interests; Warhammer 40k, Cold War, Modern Warfare, Zombie Apocalypse, etc.

Is it a bit clunky and awkward at times? Yeah, but the previous entries of Men of War and Call to Arms were WAY clunkier. Is it punishing? Oh yeah, but in a way that feels organic and fair. It does still suffer my biggest critique/gripe I had with Call to Arms; the AI is a bit more A than I and, in return, they get WAY more units than you are allotted. But the AI is smarter in this game, as well as more capable, and the disproportionate amount of units they get isn't AS ballbreaking as previous entries.

All-in-all, I'd recommend RTS lovers get it. If it's on sale, even better. PvP with friends or randos online. Or enjoy PvE gamemodes. Or, if you prefer to fly solo, the Campaign is fun and at least mildly-immersive. Plus, Conquest mode is fun and challenging with endless varieties of ways to progress through the tech trees. And if it even starts to feel remotely bland, grab a mod or two and have the whole thing renewed.

很早之前就买了的游戏，最近刚玩，从上周末开始到今天一共7天左右，我已经玩了35个小时，由此可见多么上头。
游戏玩起来像英雄连+战争之人，单位有弹药限制，坦克有甲弹对抗，还能第一人称微操单位，完美完成了我小时候兵人对抗的梦想，按常理这理应是一款完美无瑕的作品，但还是有一点瑕疵的。
首先是游戏的优化问题，我5060+9700x+ddr5 32g的配置下中画质在征服模式下人多经常会掉到50帧数左右，问题就是在单位一多的情况下显存内存显卡根本不会满载，显卡内存占用大概只有50%，显存60%长期玩起来真的很不舒服。
其次是游戏完全没有对高分辨率的优化，2k的ui非常非常小，而且完全没有相关mod，只有一个改善字体排列的mod,且只是从完全不能直视到了能玩的地步，4k字体更是想都不敢想。
以及游戏性的问题，ai真的很傻，一条路上甚至不能两辆坦克并肩前行，因为ai会傻傻的跟在前面一辆屁股后面慢吞吞的行驶，导致部队转移时效率极差，还有很多就不一一列举了。
最后是游戏性问题，我只是新手，如有错误请见谅。
游戏中甲弹对抗经常会出现敌我实力不平均，我方打不动敌方单位，即使在穿深够的情况下对比敌方坦克也需要好几发才能将其成员组击杀，或击毁。而ai轻而易举就能将你坦克成员组随意击杀，同样的122㎜榴弹炮，敌方只需一发就能将我一辆豹式成员击杀，而我炮轰几回都无法做到😅我知道游戏中存在弱点这样的机制，但是我方为什么不能轻而易举将敌方击杀?我知道能手操，可这是一款rtt类型的游戏，经常手操只会更加的手忙脚乱。
实话实说的讲，以上的缺点除开优化都是我能接受的，如果这游戏优化再好一点，我能打出五星评价。总之，这是一款非常值得推荐的作品，因为真的很好玩。

Holy buggy jesus. 

CTA: GoH (IMO), is a very satisfying and exciting RTS. It has plenty of unit micro managing, player assisted controls somewhat making up for poor unit AI; okay damage models with destructive environments, and some building elements. (I do love the persisting damage to maps on conquest; e.g. all dead vehicles, building destruction, explosion deformations, and things previously built, will stay through the entire conquest campaign, assuming you revisit said map.)
Friendly AI is pretty stupid, you may end up losing units to dumb movements or friendly fire- as I have plenty of times.
I spend most of my time ensuring units are where they should be, rotated towards X direction, or behind the correct cover. PSA: HOLD POSITION, does not. If you assign a group of vehicles to "1", and tell them to goto a location, they'll all fight over the tiny dot, wherever you placed it- often killing those poor trailered units in the process (Or knocking over an ammo truck and it going nuclear...). It should definitely allow you to line up any vehicle or artillery groups similar to infantry, but- nah. (Unit travelling trails and end locations persisting on the map may help with that, but it only appears when you've selected a specific unit or group, disappearing when selecting another.)

Conquest is something I can dump many hours in, but I feel like I'm hitting the eventual wall of experimenting with unit choices and falling into needing at least: X, Y, & Z for defense and for attack, with little room for change. Maybe I need to continue testing other ideas, unit placements, and play styles. So far I've ran many conquests with USA & The Soviet Union, finishing their tech trees, and fighting often the same kind of battles until the conquest campaign is finished- though there's the other armies and difficulties I've yet to explore too.

I very much enjoy the game, but I do wish for the previously mentioned to be improved significantly. 
If you like RTS, especially centered around WW2, I think you'll eventually enjoy this- once you've worked past some of the headaches and high costs (Sales do help). 

P.S. Conquest COOP does exist, and it was fun to destroy some enemies with a friend or 2- though the setup for it is a bit annoying and tedious, especially when defending with time management being extremely important.

The mechanics of the multiplayer mode also directly work against Axis. The game is based on quickly capturing points (flags) on the map. Early Stage Pressure: Thanks to the cheap, fast Soviet vehicles with front-loading ammo sectors and cheating in-game save codes, writing points on the map are immediately blocked. The German player loses their point advantage until they win expensive, handheld vehicles. In the end, time runs out while they're trying to clear that cheap Soviet spam. Unfortunately, these differences have made the system completely entrenched on the official servers, and the vanilla (mod-free) game has no intention of improving it.
Artificial Range Advantage: The game engine automatically assigns an extra range advantage to weapons with higher muzzle velocity. This means that a Soviet 122mm can hit you from a blind spot on the map that you can't see, while your higher-caliber or heavier German gun is forced to move to the middle of the map due to its insufficient range, essentially making itself a target.

Accuracy Nerf and Area Effect Gamble - Developer Admission: In the past, under the pretext of PvP player complaints, the accuracy rates (spread circle) of German mortars and artillery were severely undermined. Comparison: When a German gun fires, the circle where the projectile lands spreads over a huge area, and the projectile lands right next to the tank or artillery piece you're aiming at, dealing zero damage (or only track damage). In contrast, Soviet high-caliber (e.g., 280mm BR-5) or 122mm guns, having both a narrower dispersion circle and a wider coded high-explosive (HE) blast radius, could destroy a German howitzer in a single shot, even if they didn't achieve a direct hit

Multiplayer currently has serious issues.
It’s nice that the game supports online P2P lobbies, but players should have more connection options. Right now there is no LAN support and no official dedicated servers, which causes lag, desync, and poor performance in many matches — especially in larger battles.

Please give players the ability to choose between:

P2P hosting
LAN multiplayer
Dedicated/Official servers

A lot of multiplayer problems come from the host system. If the host has bad FPS, weak internet, or high ping, the entire match becomes unstable for everyone. This is very frustrating in competitive and co-op games.

Adding dedicated servers or at least LAN / Direct IP support would greatly improve stability, reduce latency, and help the game’s long-term multiplayer community.

The gameplay itself is amazing, but the networking system feels outdated for a modern RTT game.
